scope: Pinned Apache4.3.1/JDK21.0.12.1 asynchronous producer, manual receipt audit and shared result packaging; diagnostic driver qualification only.
toolchain: Rust unchanged, latest stable1.99 only; Java peer pinned JDK21.0.12.1 compiler/runtime
native_peer: Apache Kafka4.3.1 verified official distribution / RF1 / minISR1 / loopback / two topic partitions
independent_audits: Stored segment compression IDs, CRC32C and exact record counts
first_failures: Distribution kafka-clients jar differs from Maven release pin and was rejected; the exact pinned Maven jar was used.
Host JDK lacks release21 cross-compilation symbols. Same pinned JDK21 compiler uses -source21 -target21 instead; no cross-JDK build claim.
Actual current SDK deprecated consumer.close(Duration); strict build rejected it. CloseOptions.timeout replaced it.

The first complete broker negative exposed missing required error.name in failed results. Original failed attempt/raw data retained; final schema validation succeeds for both successful and failed attempts.
One checker invocation used --json as a path option; exit2 retained, corrected --output invocation passes.
limits: No frozen campaign, statistical speed comparison, world ranking, production soak or Suite HOLD change.
Driver is a named pipelined producer diagnostic, not a synchronous one-record benchmark. Latency is admission-attempt to completion, including backpressure; no open-loop claim.

Byte-based batching has no record-count cap; seeded-ID keys do not match frozen null/UUID distribution. All applicable frozen cells explicitly excluded for this driver, not claimed as SDK capability limits.
TLS/SASL, transactions, groups/share, null-key ID audits, open-loop and standalone timed fetch are unsupported; manual consumption is receipt validation only.
Zstd level3/JNI/backend pins work in actual roundtrip; required zstd comparison still needs retained encoded corpus and matching peer backend campaign.
Process CPU/RSS cover entire JVM run; allocation, average RSS and broker resources unmeasured. Host OS/JDK install is not a hermetic image.

Older failed build input sources are available only where actually retained; no reconstructed snapshot is represented as an executed source. Future build attempts freeze inputs before toolchain/dependency/compiler checks.
Unchanged dependency jars are retained once in validation/retained-build; older attempt manifests/logs/class archives remain, without duplicate jar copies.
